_comment: CANONICAL HAND-AUTHORED FORM CONFIG — the fixture behind the Part B §4 parity proof.
This is what an engineer would write by hand, exactly as they would write it. Three
independent consumers must agree on it, and the whole point is that they are checked
against THIS file rather than against each other's assumptions:
1. prisma/parity-form-builder.ts  — replays the Form Designer's authoring gestures
(makeField / insertAt / setAt / fromEditable) and asserts the schema it produces
deep-equals `schemaJson` below. This is the proof that the Builder is a UI over
the config model and not a second system.
the engine's publish gate and compute the expected values. A Builder that produced
config the engine rejects would be worse than no Builder.
3. Any human reading it — it is deliberately plain JSON with no generated noise.
Shape chosen to exercise everything Part B claims: a repeatable table, a conditionally
required field, and two calculated fields where one reads the other (which forces the
engine's dependency ordering rather than schema order).
If you change this file, all three consumers must be re-run. That coupling is the feature.
